title: The welcome page's hover sound cannot start before the first click, tap or key: the browser's rule, not the page's
context: Owner, 2026-10-07: 'landing page pocket guide: sound fx and visual on hover; the sound only triggers after something has been clicked the first time. It should trigger right away on hovering.'
outcome: Not changed. Every browser refuses to start audio until the page has had a user activation, and the activating events are mousedown/pointerdown (Chrome), pointerup/touchend/click and keys; hovering (pointerenter, mousemove) is not one. The sound engine (src/audio.js) builds its context on the first such gesture anywhere on the page, and the start gate's hover (src/fx/start-gate.js hear) plays once sfx.ready, so the first click or key anywhere, not a particular button, unlocks it; the eager context was tried before and dropped (Safari reports a context created outside a gesture as running and outputs nothing). Chrome does allow sound without a gesture on two paths outside the page's control: a same-origin navigation after a gesture on the previous page (a reload after a click), and a site whose media engagement score is high, which is why the owner sometimes hears the hover at once. Lab 144's ALL SYSTEMS NOMINAL on the START button's hover (2026-10-07-the-owners-lab-lines-wired) lives under the same rule.
alternatives: Creating the audio context at load and resuming it on hover: Chrome keeps it suspended until a gesture, and Safari's silent-running context was the 2026-10-04 bug
evidence: src/audio.js ARM_EVENTS / CREATE_EVENTS and their comments; src/fx/start-gate.js hear()
